# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the building and date of inspection.
3. Record each inaccessible area, including location and specific deficiencies.
4. Describe the problem in detail (e.g., inadequate ramp slope, lack of handrails, too-narrow doors).
5. Use precise measurements when applicable (e.g., 1-inch door threshold, 10% ramp slope).
6. List the applicable accessibility standard violated (e.g., ADAAG, IBC, local code).
7. Note any safety hazards resulting from the inaccessibility.
8. Include any photographs or diagrams supporting your observations.
9. Record witnesses or stakeholders who were present for the inspection.
10. Enter any immediate actions taken or recommended fixes.
11. Include reference to relevant compliance documents (code sections, regulations, standards).
12. Provide a summary of overall building accessibility compliance.
13. Sign the report, verifying the accuracy of the information.
14. Archive the report according to local regulations and organizational policies.
15
